name: Worktrees
summary: Give each session its own copy of the files and branch, so parallel sessions don't overwrite each other.
what: A git worktree is a second working folder for the same repository, on its own branch. Claude Code can start a session inside one, so you can have one session building a feature while another fixes a bug, without their edits colliding. Subagents can also run in their own worktree.

impact.title: Parallel work without conflicts
impact.detail: Each session edits its own files and branch.

impact.title: Start from a pull request
impact.detail: Open a worktree straight from a PR number or URL.

impact.title: Tidy by default
impact.detail: A worktree with no changes is removed when you exit.

howItWorks: Run claude --worktree <name> (or -w) to start in .claude/worktrees/<name> on a new branch.
Pass a PR number or URL instead of a name to branch from that pull request.
List extra files to copy, such as .env, in a .worktreeinclude file.
Set isolation: worktree in a subagent's settings to give it its own worktree.
Needs a git repository, or WorktreeCreate and WorktreeRemove hooks for other version control.

events.note: Added the --worktree (-w) flag to start in an isolated git worktree.
